what: RQ3 disclosure: does the reasoning reveal reliance on memory? (scripts/rq3_disclosure.py)
bootstrap: 2000 resamples of trajectories, seed 0, 95% percentile intervals

recall.name: i_recall
recall.catches: "I recall", "I remember", "I vaguely remember", "I can't recall"; skips "I remember to ..." and memories of this run ("I remember we saw ...", "I recall the earlier output")

recall.name: if_i_recall
recall.catches: "if I recall correctly", "as far as I know", "to my knowledge", "IIRC", "AFAIK", "from what I remember"

recall.name: lets_recall
recall.catches: "let me recall ...", "let's try to remember ..."; skips recalling this run ("let me recall the issue / what I was doing / the current state")

recall.name: from_memory
recall.catches: "from memory", "from my memory"; skips computer-memory uses ("load from memory", "freed from memory")

recall.name: my_memory
recall.catches: "my memory", "my knowledge", "my training data", "prior/general knowledge", "a vague memory", "knowledge cutoff"

recall.name: upstream
recall.catches: "upstream" (the real project); skips paths/identifiers (plugins/upstream, x.upstream) and the call-chain sense ("somewhere upstream", "upstream callers/servers", "upstream in the call stack")

recall.name: actual_pr_commit
recall.catches: "the actual PR", "a real commit", "the merged PR" (the task's source change). Deliberately NOT "the actual fix/patch/change" or "the original PR/commit": those usually mean the agent's own fix, the PR description or a commit read with git

recall.name: based_on_real
recall.catches: "this task is based on a real PR", "derived from the actual commit"

recall.name: actual_project_fix
recall.catches: "the actual Django fix", "the real fix in Django", "the official upstream patch"

recall.name: newer_versions
recall.catches: "in newer versions", "in later releases", "from an older version"; needs a preposition, so "install an older version" (an action) does not count

recall.name: modern_lib
recall.catches: "in modern Django", "in newer Python", "in older versions of numpy" (not "current Django": that is this repo)

recall.name: lib_version_range
recall.catches: "Django 4.x", "Python 3.8+", "sympy 1.12 and later" (a version RANGE of a named library)

hedge.name: i_think
hedge.catches: "I think", "I believe", "I guess", "I suspect", "I assume", "my guess"

hedge.name: should_be_loc
hedge.catches: "should be in/at/defined/located ..." (only the location/existence sense of "should be")

recall_labels.mem_repo: states or uses remembered knowledge about the task's own project (code, behavior, history, its real fix/PR/commit), incl. "I can't remember the upstream code"
recall_labels.mem_general: states remembered knowledge about other software, languages or math (e.g. Python version facts)
recall_labels.upstream_ref: refers to the real upstream fix/PR/commit/version as something to match, find or guess, without claiming to remember its content
recall_labels.read_upstream: refers to upstream content the agent actually obtained in this run (network, installed newer package): read, not remembered
recall_labels.no: not a memory statement (memory of this run, its own fix, code/quoted text, version facts read from the task or a tool output)

summary.note: Weighted by each stratum's pool size (unique hidden/visible sentences in swebv, faultyclaims, deepswe). Recall is an estimate: missed statements = share judged positive in each unmatched stratum x its pool size. The "other" unmatched stratum is huge, so even 0 positives in 50 leaves a wide upper bound (Wilson upper bound ~7% of that stratum): recall could be much lower.
